title: How Iran’s drones hit America’s Achilles heel
gist: Politico reports that despite eight months of US and Israeli strikes, Iran's low-cost Shahed drones continue to constrain US forces, keeping the Navy out of friendly Middle East ports, damaging a US airbase and forcing the evacuation of all US bombers from RAF Fairford. Officials warn US and European militaries are unprepared for cheap drone warfare, including 'drone terrorism' against infrastructure.

insights.claim: Despite eight months of US and Israeli attacks and Trump's claim that Iran's military is 'completely destroyed', Iran continues striking with low-cost Shahed drones that have kept the US Navy from returning to friendly Middle East ports and severely damaged a US airbase near Iran.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Iran retains asymmetric capability to disrupt Gulf operations, sustaining regional risk premia.
insights.quote: Tehran continues to strike back with low-cost Shahed drones that have kept the Navy from returning to U.S.-friendly ports in the Middle East

insights.claim: Warnings about Iranian drones led to the evacuation of all US bombers from Britain's Fairford air base and forced Trump into a catering cart in July as he left a NATO summit in Ankara.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Drone threats now reach European bases and senior leaders, broadening demand for counter-drone protection.

insights.claim: The article argues cheap drones and off-the-shelf technology are transforming warfare and that US and European officials are unprepared for this new kind of warfare.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Supports a structural spending shift toward counter-drone and base defense capabilities across NATO.
insights.quote: just how unprepared U.S. and European officials are to tackle a new kind of warfare

insights.claim: A senior European defense official warns of growing 'drone terrorism' risk from semi-organized groups and individuals attacking infrastructure with cheap, even household-made means.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Critical infrastructure operators face rising physical security costs from drone threats.
insights.quote: “What worries me is a growing possibility of ‘drone terrorism’ and ability of different semiorganized groups and vile individuals to act against our infrastructure by cheap, even household made, means,”
